label: Person
name: Adam Stanisław Grabowski
summary:
Adam Stanisław Grabowski (1698–1766) was a Polish Catholic bishop and statesman who served as Bishop of Warmia (Ermland) — one of Poland's most strategically significant dioceses, an ecclesiastical enclave surrounded by Prussian territory. He later served as Bishop of Chełmno (Kulm) and as a royal administrator (starost) combining ecclesiastical and secular governance in the manner typical of the Polish noble ecclesiastical elite.

Warmia was a unique diocese in eighteenth-century Poland: it was the diocese where Copernicus had been a canon, and it was entirely surrounded by Prussian Brandenburg territory, making its bishop's loyalty to the Polish crown a constant political question. Grabowski's tenure at Warmia came during the period of growing Prussian power under Frederick the Great, when the diocese's status was an active diplomatic issue.

His career illustrated the intersection of Polish noble identity, ecclesiastical office, and royal administration that characterised the eighteenth-century Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's governing class. As a bishop-nobleman he served at the intersection of Church and state in a constitution that blurred the boundaries between spiritual and secular authority, and his administration of both dioceses and secular starosties exemplified the hybrid nature of Polish ecclesiastical governance before the partitions.
